objective: Review the capability registry commit on release/0.3.1/feat/capabilities in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-cap against the merge-ready bar.
scope: Range: git -C /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-cap diff 5d2bed8..HEAD (one commit). The registry is packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts; form detection is setup/form.ts; setup/doctor/TUI wiring in setup/ and cli/setup.ts; pi/tools.ts; integrations/pi/src/agents.ts.

Maintainer requirements (verbatim): "everything should be modular and easily upgradeable btw" and "btw we shall support both headless use and normal use, that's the point of capabilities, to modularly support systems". Scope: move the seven existing optional capabilities onto the registry with unchanged behavior and defaults; headless/normal detection with an override; a flag and a TUI row per capability; doctor health per capability; no version outside config/pi-packages.json; no new 0.3.1 capabilities.

Behavior changes the writer reported, judge each: headless machines (CI, cloud session, Linux without a display) no longer get computer-use and setup removes a listed package; doctor lines renamed (pi features -> pi base packages, pi form, pi capability <name>); the setup screen now opens whenever Pi is in use and pi.enable is on (skipped for --undo, cloud sessions and capability flags), not only when T3 has work; setup --undo leaves capability choices in config; a user-level computerUse false beats a project-level on.

Check that a 0.3.0 config decodes and behaves the same, that the setup screen never opens without a TTY or in scripted runs, that headless detection cannot misfire on a normal desktop (Windows, macOS, Wayland), Effect and Schema rules from .claude/CLAUDE.md, JSDoc, and that tests would fail without the change. Run the built-in /code-review on the range and classify its findings.
constraints: Do not check out other commits in any checkout and make no edits.
Report in under 400 words; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking with file and line.

criteria.text: Registry-driven behavior is correct and existing defaults and 0.3.0 configs behave unchanged except the stated changes
Headless detection and the setup screen trigger are safe on every supported platform and in non-interactive runs
Tests cover the change and fail without it

result:
result: No blockers; all three criteria met. `mise run verify` passes on c001260b. The built-in review's findings are all non-blocking.
changed: none
checks: `bunx --no-install mise run verify` in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-cap -> exit 0. Type-check clean, lint clean, format clean, 2757 pass / 0 fail.

Built-in `/code-review`:
The first run read the main checkout, because the Skill tool cannot set a cwd. There HEAD is an ancestor of 5d2bed8, so the scope was empty and it returned `[]`.
The second run used the explicit SHA range `5d2bed8d...c001260b` and returned 7 findings. All are classified below.

blockers: none

findings (all non-blocking, one verdict each):
1. packages/runtime/src/setup/capabilities.ts:48-55, pi-check.ts `loadPiConfig` — optional. A `--computer-use on --scope project` choice ignores the user-file off-lock (config/load.ts:51). It writes the project file and the overlay installs the package and its no-prompt settings, while the merged config still resolves to off. I confirmed this by reading the code. It is a hole in the lock for an explicit user flag. Fix: refuse or warn when the merged value is locked off.
2. setup/steps.ts (capability step, around line 200) — optional. If `applyCapabilityChoices` fails on a write error, the package and settings steps still run with the overlay, and the packages change without the config being persisted. The built-in's example (`pi` not an object) is wrong, because the install step would fail to load that config too. Only the write-error case is real.
3. setup/form.ts:detectForm — optional. `CI=0` or `CI=no` is treated as CI and gives the headless form on a desktop. Tests cover only `false` and empty. Fix: accept only truthy values.
4. setup/pi-install.ts:112 — rejected as a defect, because it is the stated behavior. Headless detection (ssh without DISPLAY, CI) makes setup remove the computer-use package. Windows and macOS always count as having a display, and Wayland-only is covered through `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. Detection cannot misfire on a normal desktop. The `toolArgs` pattern in pi/tools.ts is not form-aware, but I found no harm in that.
5. config/capabilities.ts — optional. `skills`, `mcpServers`/`McpServer` and `FEATURE_DEFAULTS` have no consumer (grep confirmed). `applicability` is only printed by doctor. This is speculative surface, so drop it or wire it up.
6. setup/tui/session.ts:`runInteractive` — optional. The config is loaded about four times per run and `piInUse` is probed twice. Load once and pass it down.
7. setup/pi-check.ts (`checkCapabilities`) — rejected. A forced `--form normal` on a headless host fails doctor on the display need; that is the intended check.

Other points:
0.3.0 compatibility: key set, defaults and package order are unchanged. The schema is strict, and tests/config/capabilities.test.ts:83 and :110 pin both.
Setup screen: a non-TTY, CI, TERM=dumb or flagged run never opens it, because `tuiFallbackReason` runs before the load. The side effect is that a scripted run with Pi in use now prints a `~ t3 tui:` fallback line even with no T3 work. This is hint-only (optional).
Tests: the new registry, form, capabilities and TUI tests assert behavior that did not exist on the base.
I read but did not run the real-TTY screen and ssh/Wayland paths.

evidence:
Registry-driven behavior is correct and existing defaults and 0.3.0 configs behave unchanged except the stated changes: config/schema.ts and tools.ts diffs, tests/config/capabilities.test.ts:83,110, verify exit 0.
Headless detection and the setup screen trigger are safe on every supported platform and in non-interactive runs: setup/form.ts:35-60 (win32 and darwin are normal; DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY on Linux), setup/tui/session.ts `tuiFallbackReason` order, tests/setup-form.test.ts and tests/setup-tui-cli.test.ts. Only the optional `CI=0` finding (3) remains.
Tests cover the change and fail without it: new tests/config/capabilities.test.ts, setup-capabilities.test.ts, setup-form.test.ts and setup-tui-capabilities.test.ts, plus updated setup-pi.test.ts. All pass. Gaps are only `CI=0` and the lock case (1).
findings: items 1-7 above.
